corpus/ is the screen text the recogniser is measured on: each NAME.png
beside NAME.txt, the text it shows, exactly. Lines are drawn with their
baselines 1.25 line heights apart and a margin of one font size around
the block.

The text is lys's own strings, a short terminal session and the first
paragraph of the US Declaration of Independence (public domain). The
images are lys's, under its MIT licence.

ui-geist-1x, ui-geist-2x, ui-geist-dark-1x, ui-geist-bold-1x
  lys UI strings drawn by lib/render in Geist (ui/internal/uifont, SIL OFL
  1.1). Sizes: 14 px, 28 px, 13 px light-on-dark, and 14 px at wght 600,
  a weight the test does not hand the reader.

ui-cantarell-1x
  The same strings in Cantarell 15 px (lib/render's fixture face, SIL
  OFL 1.1).

term-geistmono-1x
  A terminal session in Geist Mono 14 px, light on dark, drawn by
  lib/render with the face's programming ligatures, as lys draws them.

page-inter-1x
  The paragraph in Inter 15 px (lib/inter, SIL OFL 1.1), the shape of
  a browser page.

xrender-inter-1x, xrender-geistmono-1x
  Four lines of the paragraph in Inter 15 px with full hinting, and
  four lines of the session in Geist Mono 14 px with no hinting. Both
  are drawn by golang.org/x/image/font/opentype rather than by lys's
  rasteriser.

pdf-reading-p1, -p2, -p3
  The three pages of desktop/docrender/testdata/reading.pdf, rendered by
  docrender (folio) at 96 dpi (816x1056) and cropped to x 64-480. They
  are set in folio's substitute for the non-embedded Helvetica, a face
  the reader is not given. The text is docrender's text layer for the
  page.

Baseline: tesseract 5.5.4 (`tesseract stdin stdout -l eng` on the image
upscaled 2x, as lys-shell ran it) reads this corpus at a 0.79% character
error rate (16 of 2034 characters, all in term-geistmono-1x). The rate
is the rune Levenshtein distance over the text's length, with every
line trimmed, runs of white space made one space and blank lines
dropped. The reader must stay at or below that rate.
